{"self_assessment": "Impact: I turned Leo's fish idea into a concrete plan within the first minute. I sketched the pad with the numbered strokes, which gave the table one shared blueprint to build from. I then laid the nose and top body line myself, plus the connecting runs into the junction. The body outline is the part that makes the picture read as a fish, and it fell with the push.

Execution: I worked quietly and steadily. I laid my strokes in short, consistent batches and started each one a hand's width short of the line it grew from, so I didn't disturb anyone else's work. I made the joins at the junction, where the top body meets the tail. I also inspected the junction and the tail area repeatedly. That kept the table's picture of what was connected current and helped the others decide where to put their hands.

Collaboration: I split the strokes across the table at the start so all four of us could build at once, and each person took a stroke that suited them. I kept clear of teammates' zones while they worked, particularly around the tail corner. I offered to clear the stray dominoes crowding Maya's join, and I let her lead that area.

Leadership: I helped get the table moving quickly. I backed Leo's fish idea, drew it up, and assigned the pieces so nobody waited on anyone. Once the body was in, I stopped adding dominoes and kept my hands off it, so the part that already worked stayed intact for the push. I stayed calm through the final minutes.", "my_share_percent": 30}
